correctness.rationale: The level-rank proof is valid. Noncollapsed source levels have strictly increasing minimum target ranks; hence n>m forces a collapsed level. A collapsed level makes the simplicial image a cone, so the induced sphere map is null-homotopic. For n=m, absence of a collapse forces every level to map bijectively to the matching target level, hence a homeomorphism; a collapse again gives nullity. For n<m, pi_n(S^m)=0, and a level swap realizes degree minus one while the identity realizes degree plus one.

originality.rationale: The final claim is already covered by published SCOPE results. Cross-height nullity for finite weak-order pseudospheres proves every map is null-homotopic whenever the numbers of levels differ, directly covering X_n to X_m for n not equal to m. For equal dimensions n at least two, the published exact self-homotopy classification proves every nonhomeomorphism is finite-space null-homotopic and every homeomorphism is isolated; this is stronger than the submitted order-complex conclusion. The n=1 four-point circle endpoint is covered by the published crown self-map classification, which gives winding degrees minus one, zero and one with nonzero classes exactly the automorphisms. Thus the whole stated map-rigidity theorem is a union of prior published results, not merely overlapping wording.
